title: Entrusted (Kern ch. 27)
hook: the Buddha entrusts the teaching to the bodhisattvas; the Lotus closed

segments.voice: Yesterday, Samantabhadra promised to come on a white elephant to anyone who keeps the sutra. Your line: kept and protected.

A set of keys passes from one hand to another. A night nurse walks the morning shift through each patient's chart. A shop changes hands, and the old owner stands in the doorway one last time. Handing something over is its own small ceremony, and the Lotus Sutra ends with one. In the last chapter of Kern's ordering, the Buddha rises from his seat, turns to the great crowd of bodhisattvas, and gives them the teaching to carry.
screen: `KEYS, A CHART, A SHOP.` → `HANDING OVER IS A CEREMONY.` → `THE LOTUS ENDS WITH ONE.`

segments.voice: Here's the scene, paraphrased. The Buddha stands, and by his power he reaches out his right hand to the bodhisattvas. Over ages beyond counting, he says, I worked to reach this supreme awakening. Now I hand it to you. Take it, keep it, and make it known widely, so that all beings may hear it. The bodhisattvas bow, filled with joy, and answer together: we will do as the Lord commands. Do not be concerned. And they say it again. Then the Buddha sends home the Buddhas who had gathered from other worlds to hear him, and the assembly rejoices. That's how the Lotus closes, in Kern's order: not with a final parable, but with a handoff. The teaching doesn't stay with the teacher. Look back at the whole Lotus now. A ray of light from the Buddha's brow. Skillful means and one vehicle. A burning house, a lost son, rain falling on every plant. A phantom city to rest in, and a jewel sewn in a coat. A stupa in the sky, and the dragon king's daughter. Bodhisattvas rising from the cracks of the earth, and a Buddha whose life is long beyond counting. Never Disparaging, bowing to everyone. Guanyin hearing cries. Two sons leading a king, and Samantabhadra's promise. And at the end, a hand held out to the listeners: this is yours now.
screen: `THE BUDDHA RISES FROM HIS SEAT.` · `TAKE IT, KEEP IT, MAKE IT KNOWN.` · `WE WILL DO AS THE LORD COMMANDS.` · `THE WHOLE LOTUS, LOOKED BACK ON.` · then, large: `ENTRUSTED.`

segments.voice: Think of one thing you've been holding alone: a task, a family story only you remember, a way of making something. Bring to mind someone who could hold it, and picture handing it over, your hands empty afterward. Notice whether you want to take it back; nothing needs deciding now.
Entrusted. The Lotus closes with the Buddha handing the teaching to the bodhisattvas: take it, keep it, make it known. Today's word.
Your line: entrusted. Tomorrow, a step back to look at the rest of the shelf. The Lotus is closed.

howItsDone: Communities that keep the Lotus Sutra read its entrustment as the Buddha handing the teaching to the bodhisattvas, and some readers treat reciting, copying or teaching the sutra as a way of taking up that charge.

chat.says: How does the Lotus Sutra end? With one last big parable?
options: No, with a handoff: the Buddha gives the teaching to the bodhisattvas to keep and share.
Yes, with a final parable that sums up every story the sutra told before it.
No, it ends with the Buddha passing away in front of the whole assembly.
chat.meaning: In Kern's order the Lotus closes not with a parable but with the Buddha entrusting it: take it, keep it, make it known.

Kern.meaning: Hendrik Kern, whose 1884 English Lotus Sutra orders the chapters here

bodhisattvas.meaning: beings on the path to awakening for the sake of all others

notes: Entrustment paraphrased from Kern (1884) ch. 27, not quoted. Confirm: the Buddha rises, by his power takes the bodhisattvas by the right hand / lays his right hand on them (Kumarajiva: strokes their heads three times; left out), the charge to keep and spread, the bodhisattvas' joint answer repeated, the visiting Buddhas dismissed.
'Over ages beyond counting I worked to reach this awakening' is a paraphrase; confirm the sense.

Placement claim: in Kumarajiva's Chinese (T 262) the entrustment is ch. 22, directly after the chapter on the Tathagata's supernatural power; in the Sanskrit and Kern it is last. Confirm, and confirm 'chanted across much of East Asia' for Kumarajiva's version.
Block look-back names days 1150–1183 by their index titles; confirm it matches the scripts as written.
howItsDone: 'many East Asian Buddhists recite, copy or teach it' is a general reception claim; soften or confirm.
